limitations: One organization and promo grant, either lifetime (null expiry, symbolic -1) or a finite window ending at tick2; clock0..3 with start at1; one revocation/policy-generation advance, one cache-shape corruption and at most two exact-stamp admission callbacks.

The cache validator retains finite start/expiry and provenance constraints while allowing a null lifetime expiry. Grant-specific acceptance additionally compares the supplied stamp with the current primary policy under its organization lock. Revocation changes the primary grant source and generation; an old lifetime stamp can remain structurally valid but cannot authorize another grant-specific callback. Refresh after revocation does not restore the revoked grant.

The existing24 PGlite scenarios run against actual subscription migrations and repository redemption/revocation, quota-policy reads, stamp validator and inference snapshot validator. The lifetime case now also calls real withOrganizationPolicyAdmission after revocation with the old structurally valid stamp and proves typed ORGANIZATION_POLICY_STALE before its callback runs. The strict existing Cloud hook checks every concrete test identity and zero skips.

This is a finite cache-provenance/primary-comparison projection, not a refinement proof or full inference/payment authority model. All other exact stamp fields are fixed matching values; malformed field bytes are one invalid-shape class. The model covers the grant-specific callback, not all possible organization funding sources. Multiple organizations/grants, real Postgres concurrent locks, allowance amounts and calendar replenishment, cache replication/TTL/gate propagation, provider effects, policy-generation overflow and external billing/credentials remain outside this case. Lifelong does not mean irrevocable. No liveness promise assumes provider success.

Weak fairness assumes refresh from the primary and eligible exact-stamp admission are retried. A live lifetime grant eventually admits or is revoked under those assumptions. Without fairness an eligible request may remain unattempted indefinitely; a stuttering counterexample is required.
